newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity hits new highs following natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity hits new highs following natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures front months hit new highs Wednesday on below-normal temperatures in the U.S. Northwest and an influence from surging natural gas prices, industry sources said.
Natural gas futures, reaching towards historical highs Wednesday, were said to be having a strong pyschological impact on power futures.
"It's all gas based, compounded with the weather they are having in the (Northwest) area," said one futures broker.
The Northwest was recently hit with an early winter storm, and temperatures were expected to peak in the 30s to 50s degrees Fahrenheit range today.
As of 1230 EST, December California Oregon Border (COB) futures were trading up $1.50 at $28.75 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a COB spot contract high of $29.50.
January COB was up $1.33 at a new contract high of $25.00 per MWh.
December Palo Verde (PV) was up $2.33 at $27.75 per MWh after trading at a new contract high of $28.50, while January PV was up $1.60 at a new contract high of $24.00 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1155 EST a total of 39 COB and 23 PV contracts had traded.
COB open interest for Nov 19 rose 10 to 3,940 while PV open interest fell 13 to 2,138, NYMEX said.
